key_insight: Compact ACE and NEP potentials distilled from a fixed atomistic foundation model preserve key semiconductor-interface responses while enabling simulations several orders of magnitude faster and larger than the teacher.
engineering_relevance: Direct distillation offers a practical route to large-scale thermal and mechanical simulations of heterogeneous interfaces without target-specific teacher fine-tuning.
method: Select an EquiformerV3 teacher from 128 pretrained models across 22 families.
Distill teacher predictions into compact ACE and NEP potentials.
Compare with DFT-trained students using matched training configurations and architectures.
evidence_signal: Against DFT-trained counterparts, distilled models differ by at most 6.6% in thermal conductance for 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces and by 2.8% in tensile strength and 1.5% in loading work for 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens at 500 K.
watch_item: Committee-based selection improves high-error force fitting but does not consistently improve downstream properties, so interface-level validation remains essential.
paper_title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
